notes: The Bay Area Reporter, 8 January 1976 to 20 December 1979: the 104 issues of those years in the Internet Archive collection bayareareporter (GLBT Historical Society scans, identifiers BAR_YYYYMMDD). Method as in the 1971-1975 batch: text and leaves rebuilt from each item's _djvu.xml, read by hand with no reader pass. The numbered-address passages were clustered by address, and because the paper has grown to 40 pages an issue the clusters were read in two passes: the first 67 in full, then every cluster holding an event word (opening, opened, new, moved, formerly, fire, closed and the like), 401 of the remaining 549; plus the passages around event words with no number. Kept: a named business or institution opening, moving, closing, burning or being renamed at an address on a stated date. Not kept: owners, managers, bartenders, performers and patrons, who are named on every page; anniversaries; proposals with no outcome; campaign headquarters; classified and personal advertisements; places outside San Francisco. A number the story does not print is taken from another issue of the paper and extra.placement_note says which; the one exception is the Castro Theatre, identified by name. Supervisor Harvey Milk is named once, as the owner of Castro Camera when it moved to 2362 Market Street: a public figure, dead since 1978, whose shop is what the building is known for.

coverage.remaining: 1980 to 2005 remain: 1,289 issues in the collection, January 1980 to 28 July 2005.
coverage.note: 104 issues; 7,322 numbered-address mentions on EAS streets, 722 windows after the advertisement filter in 616 address clusters, of which 468 were read (the first 67, then the 401 holding an event word), plus 420 event-word passages, the 1976 ones read in full and the 1977-1979 ones where the word was a fire, closing, move or opening (93). 61 findings written, each quote found again in the issue's text; 9 take their number from another issue or, for the Castro Theatre, from the building's name. 49 resolved and published on 47 existing pages, 2 of them placed by hand (432 Mason on the First Congregational Church, 444 Broadway inside 438-448), 3 conflicts with context statements stated. No page seeded. 12 unresolved: 9 where the building is gone or the number falls between parcels, 1 on a condominium with no page (1287 Howard), 1 on a replaced building with no page (1523 Franklin), and the renaming of the Harvey Milk Center at 50 Scott Street, which belongs on the Duboce Park place page.
